Contract.title: Agree the wire representation of the sequence field
Contract.Problem: The canonical wire definition states the signed 64-bit sequence field as a zigzag varint of at most ten bytes. The consumer decodes it as an unsigned varint, and the producer, which holds the value as a big integer, encodes without a range test, so values near the sign and range boundaries do not survive a round trip.
Contract.Change: The wire format does not move: the canonical definition is unchanged and a conforming peer is unaffected. The consumer decodes the sequence field as the zigzag varint the definition states, and both sides reject a value outside the supported domain. The supported domain is every integer from -9223372036854775808 through 9223372036854775807. Out of domain means, on encode, an integer outside that range and, on decode, a varint longer than ten bytes or one carrying more than 64 bits.

Constraints.Constraint: Both sides take the field from the one canonical definition, wire/messages.schema.

The shared vectors hold at least these cases. Accepted, each with its exact bytes: 0, -1, 1, 9223372036854775807 and -9223372036854775808. Rejected on encode: 9223372036854775808 and -9223372036854775809. Rejected on decode: an eleven-byte varint and a ten-byte varint carrying 65 bits.

Acceptance.Criterion: Every accepted vector of K3 encodes to its stated bytes and decodes to its stated value on both sides.
Every rejected vector of K3 is refused, the encode cases by the producer and the decode cases by the consumer, and a vector marked rejected that is accepted fails the conformance command.

Decisions.Decision: If a change to the framing version or to the canonical definition proves necessary, it is a material revision of this contract and needs a new approval before any such work.
No check tests that the vectors hold the K3 cases; the owner leaves that to review of the diff.
